questionsToConsider: Which parts of your process do you want judged: goal setting, regular check-ins, formal reviews, ratings or all of them?
Should managers and employees see different questions, beyond the manager block already here?
When will you run it: straight after a review cycle, or halfway between two?
Who will own the changes, and how will you tell staff what changed?
guide.howToUseResponses: Compare the agreement grid between managers and non-managers, because a gap there often shows where the process breaks down. Look at the statements with the most disagreement first, then read the written answers from people who scored the process low to understand why. Use the manager answers to plan training or better guidance, and repeat the survey after the next cycle to see if the changes worked.
customizeSteps: Rename goals, check-ins and reviews to the terms your organisation uses, such as objectives, one-to-ones or appraisals.
Edit the agreement grid so each row matches a step in your process that you could actually change.
Send it within two weeks of a review cycle closing, while people still remember how it went.

faqs.q: What is a performance management survey?
faqs.a: A survey that asks staff how well the goal setting, feedback and review process works for them. It judges the process, not any one person's performance.

faqs.q: What questions should a performance management survey ask?
faqs.a: Whether expectations are clear, how goals are set, how often useful feedback happens, whether reviews feel fair and whether they lead to development.

faqs.q: Should a performance management survey be anonymous?
faqs.a: Yes, in most cases. This template asks only whether someone manages people, so you can compare the two groups without identifying anyone.

faqs.q: How is this different from an employee performance survey?
faqs.a: An employee performance survey is about one person's work. This one is about the system everyone goes through, so you can fix what isn't helping.
